fields.v: Ma, J., Wang, S., Kung, J. H., Chilton, L. B. (2026). Zoro: Active Controls to Support Rule Following in Vibe Coding. In The 39th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology (UIST '26), Detroit, MI, USA. ACM. doi:10.1145/3830398.3830629. arXiv:2604.15625v3 [cs.HC], 19 Oct 2026
Conference — UIST '26, 39th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology, Detroit, MI, USA, ACM, doi:10.1145/3830398.3830629; full text read from arXiv:2604.15625v3
Columbia University, New York, USA (all authors)

Proposes an approach; secondary: Evaluates — Zoro system and Enrich-Enforce-Evolve framework, evaluated by a technical evaluation with 4 conditions incl. component ablations (36 sessions) and a qualitative user study (N=12); formative interviews (N=10)
Zoro (no version; github.com/jennygzma/zoro): Enrich-Enforce-Evolve framework; zoro-cli Python package + visual interface; works with Codex, Claude Code, Cline, Cursor

Rules files (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) converted to a structured JSON ruleset (enforcement level, category, confidence, decay score, scope); agent-generated plan enriched with rules per step; ZORO.md instruction file prepended to AGENTS.md; .zoro shared directory; enforcement evidence per rule (summary, code artefact, unit test for testable rules); in-situ notes; refined rules

Agent generates plan -> Enrich (GPT-5.3 rewrites plan, decomposes steps, attaches rules, proposes enforcement level) -> user edits plan and sets enforcement (non-strict / strict / testable) -> Enforce (agent executes step by step; must call zoro prove-rule with evidence and tests before zoro update-step; CLI blocks completion if strict rules unverified) -> user reviews evidence and adds in-situ notes -> Evolve (notes aggregated, LLM proposes refined rules, user accepts/edits/rejects)

User edits enriched plan and sets enforcement levels; agent pauses for user decisions when rules require it; user reviews enforcement evidence and adds in-situ notes; user approves refined rules in a diff view (Rule Review)
Full workflow in the user study (Enrich-Enforce-Evolve); technical evaluation exercises Enrich and Enforce only

Not classifiable (rules files and per-task plans, not specifications); authors' wording: rules made 'active controls', a 'living and evolving' ruleset. If classified, the persistent, enforced ruleset is closest to spec-anchored; plans are not kept as specifications
fields.why: The paper uses no SDD terms; the artefact is a persistent rules file plus per-task enriched plans. Not classifiable fits other rule-file studies; spec-anchored is arguable for the enforced, evolving ruleset. Author's call

fields.v: Existing code bases: feature additions to full-stack repositories built by the authors (technical evaluation); user study on participants' own repositories (7) or the provided Poneglyph app (5)
Technical evaluation: 9 tasks, each 500-5,000 lines of code, in NoteSense (22k LOC) and SnakeGame (11k LOC); user study: 2 tasks per participant, 30-45 min each

Full-stack web apps (TypeScript/React, Flask or Node/Express, SQLite): note-taking/sensemaking app, browser game; user study: ML research code, graphics heatmaps, econ analysis, journaling app, iOS app

User study: 12 expert vibe coders (>=5 years coding; 8 industry engineers/analysts, 4 PhD students; 10 use rules files daily). Formative: 10 expert programmers (5-10 years). Technical evaluation: no human operator beyond minimal compile patches
Token overhead only reported qualitatively (~4x tokens for Full Zoro vs standard vibe coding); no time or money
Feature completeness (task-specific rubric, 0-1)
Rules followed (task-specific rubric: pass/fail per rule per session, any violation = not followed); by rule type (process vs coding)
fields.why: 'Rules followed' mixes coding rules (naming, API structure, formatting: internal quality) with process rules (e.g. confirm before a destructive action, run a migration, p. 8), which are agent behaviour. The author may split it or move the process part to Other outcome metrics

fields.v: User study: number of rules enforced (166, 110 unique; 9.17 per session); self-reported cognitive load; preferences
Rule pass rate in user study (Task 1 77.9%, Task 2 94.4%); refined rules re-applied correctly (12/13); qualitative themes (auditability, trust, shift to 'rule engineering')

Manual: two annotators (software engineers, >=5 years) graded code and chat history with task rubrics (Cohen's kappa 0.97 rules, 0.82 features); one-way ANOVA and Holm-Bonferroni paired t-tests. User study: think-aloud, interviews, open coding by one author refined with team

Technical evaluation. Criterion: task-specific rubrics (feature completeness; rules followed, pass/fail per rule) graded by 2 annotators. All with Cline (version not stated) + Claude Sonnet 4.6, 9 tasks, 1 run each (Table 1, mean ± 95% CI). Cost: only the ~4x token overhead of Full Zoro vs standard vibe coding is reported; no absolute tokens, time or money
- No Zoro (baseline; rules in AGENTS.md) + Cline + Sonnet 4.6: features 0.64±0.144; rules 0.51±0.08. Quality: partly (about two thirds of features, half of rules followed); cost: not measured
- Basic Zoro (ablation: mark steps, no enrich, no enforce) + Cline + Sonnet 4.6: features 0.65±0.17; rules 0.55±0.11. Quality: partly; cost: not measured
- Partial Zoro (ablation: enrich, no enforce) + Cline + Sonnet 4.6: features 0.61±0.11; rules 0.68±0.07. Quality: partly; cost: not measured
- Full Zoro (enrich + enforce) + Cline + Sonnet 4.6: features 0.77±0.13; rules 0.80±0.08; process rules 0.87, coding rules 0.75 (Appendix B.3). Quality: partly (best on both, but about 1 in 5 rules and features still missed); cost: partly (about 4x tokens of standard vibe coding)
User study (full Enrich-Enforce-Evolve + Codex, model Not stated; 12 participants, 2 tasks each; criterion: enforced-rule pass rate): 77.9% (60/77) task 1, 94.4% (84/89) task 2; 12/13 refined rules then applied correctly. Quality: partly (works by task 2); cost: not measured. No baseline
fields.why: The baseline had no verdict; Basic Zoro's 'does not work (n.s.)' was judged against the baseline, not on its own (0.65 features, 0.55 rules is partly); Full Zoro had two quality values (one is required); the user-study entry had no verdict. Values unchanged. Full Zoro quality partly vs works is a judgement (0.80 rules, 0.77 features)

fields.v: Tasks: 9 multi-step feature tasks (5 NoteSense, 4 SnakeGame), repositories and rules built by the authors. Configurations: No / Basic / Partial / Full Zoro. Baseline: No Zoro (rules only in AGENTS.md). Held constant: agent (Cline), model (Claude Sonnet 4.6), task description and development plan provided. Acceptance criteria: task rubrics graded by 2 annotators (no automated tests mentioned). Repetitions: 1 run per task per condition ('breadth rather than repeated data points'). Human intervention: minimal patches applied for compiler errors (counts recorded)

Full Zoro follows rules most: 0.80 vs 0.51 baseline (+29 pts; ANOVA p<0.05; Full significantly better than all others; Partial better than No Zoro, Holm-Bonferroni). Feature completeness 0.77 vs 0.61-0.65 (n.s.). Largest gain for process rules (35% -> 87%) vs coding rules (59% -> 75%). Cost: ~4x token usage

Distinguished conditions on rule following, not on features. Repeatability: one run per task; tasks and repos built by the authors; code open-source. Limitations stated: only 36 cases due to cost; scoped to Cline (technical) and Codex (user study); evidence is not a formal guarantee

User study: 12 sessions, two tasks, single-developer codebases; need longitudinal, more diverse studies. Technical evaluation limited to 36 cases (cost); ~4x token overhead (prompt caching, deterministic checks as remedies); enforcement evidence not a formal guarantee (over-trust risk); static rule retrieval; manual setup, cognitive load of separate interface; code/tests insufficient evidence for performance or UI rules; ruleset management (conflicts, organisation) open

Code: https://github.com/jennygzma/zoro. Table 1 values rebuilt from pdftotext text (order matched to conditions). Rubrics graded by annotators paid by the authors; feature completeness also annotator-judged, not test-based. Model used by Codex in the user study Not stated; GPT-5.3 used inside Zoro for enrichment and refinement. Number of compile patches 'recorded' but not reported. No pre-registration. Programming language: TypeScript, Python, JavaScript (full-stack apps)
